title: Turkmen movement from Iran into Armenia and Anatolia
summary: After the Seljuk victory at Dandanqan in 1040, bands of Turkmen nomads moved through Azerbaijan into Armenia, then a Byzantine possession, looking for booty. They looted Vaspurakan in 1042, Ibrahim Yinal's Oghuz force reached Malazgirt, Erzurum and Trabzon in 1048 to 1049, and Sivas was sacked in 1059, years before the 1071 battle of Malazgirt.

uncertainty.note: EBSCO: Dandanqan 1040. Bedrosian (1997): Turkmens from the Urmia area looted Vaspurakan in 1042, Baiburt 1054, Sebastia/Sivas sacked 1059. Karakök (2025) quoting Cami' al-Duwal: year 440 (1048/1049) at Malazgirt, Erzurum and Trabzon; Bedrosian dates the same expedition from 1047. The end is the last dated waypoint, not the end of the movement.

as_recorded.value: In 1042 some 15,000 Turkmens from the Urmia area attacked and looted Vaspurakan
In the year 440 (1048/1049), Turul Bey's brother brahim Yinal, with a large group of Oghuz, went to the cities of Anatolia

where.modern_name: Route from Urmia (Iran) through Erzurum and Bayburt to Sivas (Turkey)
where.historical_name: Seljuk-ruled Iran and Azerbaijan, then Byzantine Armenia and eastern Anatolia

waypoints.label: Urmia area: the starting area of 15,000 Turkmens who looted Vaspurakan in 1042.
Erzurum (Erzenu'r-Rum): reached by Ibrahim Yinal's Oghuz force after Malazgirt, on the way to Trabzon.
Baiburt (Bayburt), listed among Turkic targets in 1054.

importance.justification: The first stage of Turkic movement into Anatolia, which produced Turkic dominance there after Malazgirt.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the framing: Bedrosian and Karakök describe raids and expeditions; Karakök says populations were settled in Anatolia before 1071 but I found no page giving dated settlement stops, so the path follows dated raids. The sources date Ibrahim Yinal's march differently (Bedrosian from 1047, Cami' al-Duwal 1048/1049). Karakök calls the early raids early eleventh century, before the 1040 start I took from EBSCO. Erzurum, Bayburt and Sivas are Wikidata city points.

beats.caption: About 15,000 Turkmens from the Urmia area attack and loot Vaspurakan, defeating Byzantine forces near Arjesh on Lake Van.
Ibrahim Yinal's Oghuz force reaches Malazgirt, Erzurum and Trabzon and defeats a large Byzantine and Abkhazian army.
Turkmen raiding reaches Sebastia (Sivas), which is sacked; Turks were also being settled in Anatolia before the 1071 battle of Malazgirt.
